title: Drop an inert stale approval: the cleanup arm DEC-246 (a3) deferred past 0.1.0
description: Filed from WCLI-82 by the ward-cli worker on 2026-10-26, on the lead ruling DEC-246 (a3) Q2. Since the rv331 fix round, ward status and ward doctor name every stale approval of the current project and separate the ones that can still be cleared from the ones that cannot: a record whose checkout no longer resolves, or whose profile is no longer declared, is named inert and unreachable, and doctor no longer fails on it. That is the keep-inert arm of DEC-246 (a2) clause 3, and it is the whole of what 0.1.0 does. What is missing is any way to REMOVE such a record: re-approval is the only clearing write, and it cannot reach a checkout that is gone. DEC-246 (a3) rejected arm B, a terminal-only drop command, for 0.1.0 and allowed it to be filed as later work. That is this task. The design is not settled here: whether the answer is a drop command, a re-register-then-revoke path, or something else is a decision for opum-doc and the operator, and this task should put it there before any code lands. Binding constraint either way: clause 3 forbids a silent removal, so whatever is built must name the drop in that command output.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A recorded decision settles how an inert stale approval is removed, taken by opum-doc as the operator design delegate and carried as an ADR in this repository naming that decision id back.
No path removes an inert stale approval silently: the removal names itself in the output of the command that performed it, satisfying DEC-246 (a2) clause 3.
Removal is measured both ways in tests: a record the command is asked to remove is gone afterwards, and every record it was not asked about is still present and still inert.
The install runbook and ADR 0018 describe how an operator clears a record this build cannot clear by re-approval, once the decision exists.

implementationNotes: CANDIDATE FOR OPUM-DOC, relayed from the rv331-ward188b verdict (INFO under call (a)), not in scope for WCLI-82 at the lead ruling. The scope key that decides which stale approvals status and doctor name is the projectId this checkout's tracked manifest declares, and a manifest is repository-controlled. A repository that copied another project's projectId would therefore see that project's stale records named in its own report. What it exposes is limited: no secret, no alias, only stale approval records, and the attacker needs the other project's UUID. Closing it would mean gating the naming on the binding being registered, which is a change to what DEC-246 (a3) Q1 rules (scope by project) rather than a bug in it, so it is not ward-cli's to decide. Re-approval and any removal command are the surfaces where this matters most, which is why it is recorded here rather than on WCLI-82.
